# @forgesworn/kindred

> An app wants to hold a user's relationships — family, people they've met and
> verified, public keys they recognise — WITHOUT becoming a social network (no
> feed, no follower count, no central graph, no shadow profiles). kindred is those
> primitives as plain data + pure functions: it holds relationships across three
> social distances, runs the kith bond ceremony (byte-exact ECDH + spoken words),
> pins and live-challenges recognised keys (ken), and tests a user's own contacts
> against a server's published presence filter LOCALLY (over @forgesworn/tessera-kit). No
> storage, no UI, no graph traversal — those are explicit non-goals.

kindred is a protocol-neutral TypeScript library for VERIFIED RELATIONSHIPS:
`kin` (family — mutual + guardianship), `kith` (mutually verified via ECDH +
spoken-token words), `ken` (one-way recognised public keys). ESM-only, Node ≥ 22.
Deps: `@forgesworn/tessera-kit`, `spoken-token`, `nostr-attestations`, `@noble/*`,
`@scure/base`; peer `nostr-tools`. It is the relationships brick of the Forgesworn /
Signet ecosystem, consumed by signet-app.

## Getting Started

```
npm i @forgesworn/kindred
```

`@forgesworn/tessera-kit` is a sibling NOT YET ON NPM. For local dev, pack + install the tarball
(`cd ../tessera-kit && npm pack && cd ../kindred && npm i ../tessera-kit/forgesworn-tessera-kit-0.1.0.tgz`).
To PUBLISH kindred, publish @forgesworn/tessera-kit first — do NOT ship a `file:` dep.

```typescript
import { deriveBondSecret, bondWords, verifyBondWord } from '@forgesworn/kindred/bond'
import { pinKenFromNip05, buildKeyControlChallenge, verifyKeyControl } from '@forgesworn/kindred/ken'
import { discoverPresent, parseFilterPublication } from '@forgesworn/kindred/discovery'

// kith: derive the byte-exact shared secret, read directional words for a counter.
const secret = deriveBondSecret(myPrivHex, theirPubHex)
const { mine } = bondWords(secret, myPubHex, theirPubHex, counter)
const { ok } = verifyBondWord(secret, myPubHex, theirPubHex, counter, whatTheySaid) // → { ok }

// ken: pin (TOFU), then prove LIVE control with a fresh nonce (attribution alone is replayable).
const entry = await pinKenFromNip05('mrbeast@example.com', myPersonaPubHex, fetch)
const { nonce } = buildKeyControlChallenge()
const { ok, reason } = verifyKeyControl(entry, nonce, signedByClaimant) // → { ok, reason? }

// discovery: pin-verify the publication, then test MY contacts scoped to one persona.
const pub = parseFilterPublication(rawWireEvent)        // raw event, never spread-mutated
const present = discoverPresent(parseFilter(pub.blob), myEntries, myPersonaPubHex)
```

## Key Concepts

- **Three tiers** — `kin` / `kith` (both carry an ECDH `sharedSecret`, never
  published) / `ken` (no secret, one-way). `hasSharedSecret` narrows the union.
- **Persona scoping** — every entry has an `ownerPubkey` (one of my nsec-tree
  persona keys). `discoverPresent` throws on mixed-owner input (anti-correlation).
  Enforced where kindred can; full at-rest scoping is the consumer's obligation.
- **Byte-exact ECDH** — `deriveBondSecret` reproduces signet-protocol's
  `sha256(x-coord(myPriv · lift_x_even('02'||theirX)))` so migrated contacts' words
  don't break. Agreement holds because only x is hashed (±P share an x).
- **Directional words** — `deriveDirectionalPair` over `kindred:bond`, sorted
  `[lo,hi]` roles; `mine !== theirs`; verify re-derives + constant-time compares.
- **ken key-control vs attribution** — `verifyKeyControl` (fresh nonce) proves LIVE
  control (replay-proof); `attributeSignature` is REPLAYABLE by design (credit an
  artifact, don't authenticate a party).
- **NIP-05 = TOFU** — a DNS/TLS/HTTP trust-on-first-use anchor, NOT key-continuity;
  key changes are propose-only, never auto-flipped.
- **Corroboration** — `KenEntry.corroborations?` holds ADDITIONAL independent
  confirmations; `provenance` stays required + singular (so the field is purely
  additive and an entry without it serialises byte-identically). The
  `KenProvenance['source']` union is FROZEN: `validateProvenance` throws on an
  unknown source, so adding a value would make an older validator reject the WHOLE
  entry. Optional fields are safe; new enum values are not.
  `summarizeKenProvenance` returns FACTS (counts + timestamps), never a trust
  score — weighting channels is consumer policy, and a scalar would invite being
  used as an authorization input. It also returns `claimed`: how many records are
  RELAYED companion claims (reserved `companion:` locator prefix) rather than
  first-hand checks. Render `confirmations - claimed`, or you show claims as
  verification.
- **Consumer rule** — no app but signet-app is a source of identity truth. A
  consumer MAY hold domain relationships (who is in this community); it MUST NOT
  hold identity verification. Structural, not policy: `GrantContactView` is
  secret-stripped at the type level and a companion holds no identity keys, so it
  cannot mint kith/kin — only propose a ken, with its provenance as a CLAIM that
  `landReturnedKen` files as a namespaced corroboration, never as the primary.
- **Private annotations** — local recall aids (`groupId`/`label`/`note`/`blocked`),
  searchable in memory, NEVER serialised onto a wire (type-level + runtime); INCLUDED
  in the user's own encrypted self-backup (allowed — not a graph disclosure).
- **Discovery** — kind 30444 publication (matches @forgesworn/tessera-kit), `['n', namespace]`
  indexable tag, opt-out kind 30445. Verify BOTH the Nostr sig and the in-blob
  Schnorr sig against a pinned key before trusting any hit.

## API Surface

- `.` — model types + `EventTemplate`/`NostrEvent`/`NostrFilter` aliases +
  `hasSharedSecret`; local ops `scopeToPersona`, `assertOwnedPersona`,
  `searchEntries`, `linkForRecall`/`unlink`, `toWire`/`serializeEntry`/`parseEntry`,
  `exportEntriesEncrypted`/`importEntries`.
- `./handshake` — `buildHandshakePayload` / `parseHandshakePayload`; `HandshakePayload`.
- `./bond` — `deriveBondSecret`, `bondWords`, `verifyBondWord`, `buildBondAttestation`,
  `retractBondAssertion`, `KINDRED_BOND_NAMESPACE`.
- `./ken` — `pinKen`, `pinKenFromNip05`, `buildKeyControlChallenge`,
  `verifyKeyControl`, `attributeSignature`, `resolveKen`, `acceptKenRotation`,
  `revokeKen`, `dropKen`, `addCorroboration`, `summarizeKenProvenance`.
- `./companion-rail` — `buildPairingUri`/`parsePairingRequest`,
  `buildPairingAck`/`parsePairingAck`, `applyCompanionSnapshot`; return rail
  `WireKen`, `buildReturnEnvelope`/`parseReturnEnvelope`, `landReturnedKen`;
  `ACK_KIND`, `SNAPSHOT_KIND`, `SNAPSHOT_D_TAG`, `RETURN_D_TAG`,
  `RETURN_ADDITIONS_CAP`, `RETURN_CORROBORATIONS_CAP`.
- `./discovery` — `discoverPresent`, `disclosureFor`, `buildFilterPublication`,
  `parseFilterPublication`, `aggregatorQuery`, `buildOptOutRequest`, `parseFilter`
  (re-export); `KINDRED_FILTER_KIND`, `KINDRED_OPTOUT_KIND`.
- `./invite` — `buildJoinInvite`, `parseJoinInvite`, `verifyBondAttestation`; `JoinInvite`.

## Security

ONE-LINE CAVEAT: kindred makes narrow, honest claims — persona-scoping is a consumer
obligation it assists but cannot guarantee; NIP-05 is TOFU not key-continuity;
`attributeSignature` is replayable (use `verifyKeyControl`); annotations are never
serialised; and a forged presence filter is a doxxing primitive, so verify the Nostr
sig AND the in-blob Schnorr sig against a PINNED server key before trusting any hit.
Full posture in SECURITY.md.
